title: Gate: run the lanes that fail most often first in the release tier

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P5
labels.description: Agent surface and tooling keep up with what shipped

body:
What happens: the release tier runs its steps in a fixed order (`release_with`, `xtask/src/plan.rs`). The heavy `--ignored` release lanes run last. A full run on the cut runner takes about 91 minutes.

In the v0.23.0 cut, the two red gate results were in heavy lanes (`motion heavy`, then `app heavy: pocket3d_hsm`, #2369). Each failure showed only near the end of a run.

The maintainer asked (2026-11-17): "So.. should we check what lanes usually fails.. and make em run early?"

Work:
1. Read the `gate-logs` artifacts and the step summaries of the past `cut.yml` runs and the red `post-merge.yml` runs. Count the red steps for each lane. Known red cut runs: 43739171721, 44127297984.
2. Change the release plan order so that the lanes with the most failures run first. The first candidate is the heavy lanes, immediately after the two builds.
3. Keep the rules of `xtask/src/lanes.rs`: builds, clippy and the app, kernel and ui suites run alone.
4. Keep the step names. `--only` and `--failed` use them.
5. Optional: add an `only` input to `cut.yml` stage gate, to check one fixed step on the runner. The tag stage must still accept only a full green run.

Not in scope: an early stop on the first red step. One run must still report each failure.

Done means: the release plan runs the lanes of step 2 before the debug suites; a test in `xtask` pins the new order; the issue has the failure counts of step 1 in a comment; the step count of `gate release --dry-run` is the same before and after.

Process change: yes (`xtask/`, and `.github/workflows/cut.yml` if item 5 is done).
